newsitem.title: FRANCE: French officials decline all comment on 97 deficit.
newsitem.headline: French officials decline all comment on 97 deficit.

text.p: French government officials on Friday declined all comment on the size of the central government budget deficit next year, reiterating that the budget would be announced on September 18.
Several French newspapers have said the 1997 central government budget deficit may be between 270 billion and 280 billion francs after a forecast 288 billion in 1996.

The newspapers gave no source for their figures and it was unclear whether they had simply made an assumption based on the fact that planned income tax cuts of 25 billion francs may have to be added to the government's deficit forecast earlier this year of 248 billion francs.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has said the government will announce a deficit before tax cuts and a deficit after tax cuts.

Officials at both the finance ministry and the prime minister's office have repeatedly declined all comment on the budget ahead of its presentation, except to repeat that the total state deficit will be held within three percent of gross domestic product.

"There are all kinds of figures in the press. It does not come from the prime minister's office or from the finance ministry. We will make no comment. The figure will be announced on September 18," an official at Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office said.
"What is important it that we will reach three percent (of GDP) in 1997 after four percent in 1996," a finance ministry official said.
The total public deficit includes the central government deficit, along with deficits on welfare and local authority spending.
